Definition: apparently a primary word; a kernel of seed:--corn, grain.
KeyPassages: Matthew 13:31; Matthew 17:20; Mark 4:31; Luke 13:19; John 12:24; 1 Corinthians 15:37
BiblicalUsage: Kokkos is a grain, a kernel of seed. Matthew 13:31 and Mark 4:31 and Luke 13:19 all compare the kingdom of heaven to a grain of mustard seed, the least of all seeds that grows into a tree, Matthew 17:20 says faith as a grain of mustard seed shall move a mountain, John 12:24 says except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone, but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit, and 1 Corinthians 15:37 says that which thou sowest is bare grain, not the body that shall be.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the grain is the kingdom's whole method: the smallest seed, the dying wheat, the bare grain in the ground. I hold that nothing in the kingdom grows without dying first, and the mountain moves only for faith as small as a mustard seed.
